name: Street Custom 'Black Widow' Electronic Bait Device
product_name: Street Custom 'Black Widow' Electronic Bait Device
description: A small device that mimics the signal profile of a high-value electronic target — an unprotected neural interface, an open Diaspora node, or an unsecured corporate data terminal — to lure hackers and cyber-intruders into connecting. When a hostile operator attempts to access the fake target, the Black Widow counter-attacks through the connection, deploying malware, extracting the attacker's location and identity, or injecting a tracking payload into their neural interface. The device is essentially a digital booby trap, punishing anyone who attempts unauthorized access to what appears to be an easy target.
legality: Legal gray area — defensive countermeasure vs. offensive cyberweapon

specifications.info: Diaspora node; or data terminal signatures; identity extraction; tracking payload; concealable
specifications.programmable: Multiple trap profiles and response types

story_hooks: A Black Widow device deployed near a corporate facility caught a hacker — the counter-attack extracted their neural interface identity, revealing them as an employee of a rival corporation conducting espionage.

A network of Black Widow devices has been deployed across a district, creating a minefield for cyber-operators — anyone who scans for targets in the area risks tripping a trap that exposes their identity and location.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, predatory-looking cube with aggressive aesthetic cues. Black anodized aluminum housing with sharp, angular edges that suggest danger. The form factor evokes a spider's body — deliberately unsettling, designed to intimidate if discovered. Top surface features a recessed LED array arranged in a pattern resembling compound eyes.
physical_description.dimensions: 8cm × 8cm × 6cm (roughly a deck of cards standing on edge)
physical_description.weight_description: Pocketable — approximately 100 grams, light enough for concealment in gear or mounted under furniture
physical_description.primary_material: Matte-black anodized aluminum chassis with carbon fiber reinforcement panels
physical_description.finish: Brushed black with oil-slick iridescent accents on beveled edges; anti-reflective coating to minimize visibility in low light
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep matte black primary with crimson LED indicators and faint violet accent lines tracing circuit patterns across the surface
physical_description.interface_elements: Recessed 0.8cm touchpad on top surface (barely visible); micro-USB diagnostic port on underside (tamper-sealed); three tiny status LEDs (green standby, red active, violet intrusion detected); minimal labeling — only a stylized spider web icon embossed above the touchpad
distinctive_features: Eight symmetrically-drilled ventilation ports arranged like fangs on the front face
Soft crimson glow emanating from internal LED array when armed, visible through semi-translucent black resin accent strip
Asymmetrical weight distribution creating a naturally predatory appearance when viewed from angles
Ultra-minimal design language — almost no visible screws, suggesting sealed/irreparable construction
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tiny 'Street Custom' logo (stylized SC in angular script) etched into underside; no regulatory stamps (characteristic of Tier 2-3 street-manufacture); hand-stamped serial number suggesting small-batch production
physical_description.condition_typical: Sits inert and dark on a network perimeter, almost invisible until armed — then emits barely-perceptible crimson pulse; shows fingerprint oils and dust accumulation from field use; may have small scratches or dents from rough handling in urban environments
